summary: All three of my turn-2 findings are repaired, and I confirmed each against the frozen turn-2 subject by diff rather than against the entry's account of itself. The coordinator working notes are gone, the file terminates with a newline, and the re-measure clause I flagged as silently dropped is restored — so my non-blocking note was answered as well. The Codex turn-1 digest now reads f58dfd63…, which I re-derived by hashing the file without opening it. Both new verdict pins introduced this turn also match live bytes, including my own turn-2 verdict. The operative rider and clauses 2 and 3 do not appear in the diff at all, so the scoped removal and the arithmetic I rebuilt from D-002 and v3's gate records are byte-identical to what I already verified. Nothing blocks.

notesNonBlocking.observation: The table carries rows for D086-SF-1, D086-N-1, D086-T2-MF-1, D086-T2-MF-2, D086-T2-SF-1 and both Codex ADV IDs, but no row for my turn-2 note D086-T2-N-1, which searched zero times in the subject. The substance was nevertheless fixed: the dropped 'If a cited file moves, re-measure. Do not edit this subject after dispatch.' clause is restored verbatim at the end of the file, and the D086-T2-MF-1 row describes that restoration. So this is bookkeeping, not a gap in the repair — recorded only because turn 1's note did get its own row and the asymmetry could read as the finding having been missed rather than folded in. That same cell also spells the word 'remasure'; the operative text elsewhere spells it 're-measure' correctly. Neither observation blocks and neither needs a further turn.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 30c8a985bbd5f838d1313c2d005b12a159c7eae07216ce19228434a83d0832d6, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 058dc795… across start and end.

The entry also states explicitly that the turn-2 subject 'is not the adopting text', which is the correct disposition for a draft that was dispatched defective.

The attack 'trailing working notes remain' fails, tested by content rather than by length. I searched the raw bytes for five distinct markers from the deleted passage — 'Wait -', 'I chmod', 'Fix it', 'Let me hash' and 'accidentally' — and all five are absent. The file now ends with the re-measure clause and terminates with a newline, which I checked at the byte level; the turn-2 file did not.

The string 'fafcaf48' does not occur anywhere in the subject, and the row now reads f58dfd6395ae9300558367f1bded888c2a61a91f5969871dbba7de4b0ede6dff, which I re-derived myself by hashing coordinator-decisions.D-086.review-adversarial.codex.json without opening it — 6662 bytes, matching.

The two verdict pins introduced this turn also match live bytes, which matters because a mis-pinned peer verdict is the defect this turn exists to repair and the repair added two more of the same kind. Claude 2 turn 2 pins b85f0bcf…, equal to the file I wrote at 17591 bytes; Codex turn 2 pins e6b9ce7e…, which I confirmed by hashing at 10003 bytes without opening it. With the turn-1 pair, all four reviewer-verdict pins in the table verify.

The attack 'D086-T2-SF-1 still says already / no edit' fails. The D086-N-1 row now reads 'ACCEPTED. Clause 3 now names both denominators: owners 22 of 22 gate rows; named-harness half 0 of 18 required gates. Edited from the turn-1 wording.' The words 'already' and 'No edit' are gone and the row states the edit, which is the repair I proposed in the form I proposed it.

The attack 'D086-SF-1 unscoped again' fails, and I established this the strong way: the 'Operative rider RB-GHN-V3-A1' section does not appear in the turn-2-to-turn-3 diff at all, so it is byte-identical to the text I verified at turn 2. It still reads 'Remove the word "countable" from that sentence only' with the two v3 refusals named as retained verbatim, and the rejected alternative 'Leave "Remove the word countable" unscoped. Rejected: D086-SF-1' survives.

The attacks 'presents 16 of 16', 'counts G03/G04 as named' and 'restores G17' all fail, and again by absence from the diff rather than by re-reading. Clauses 2 and 3 are byte-identical to turn 2, so the arithmetic I rebuilt at turn 1 from D-002 and from v3's own gate records — nineteen minus G17 order-equal to v3's eighteen, eighteen minus {G03, G04} equal to sixteen — carries through unchanged. Clause 3 still reads '16 of 18, not 16 of 16, and still not MET' with both denominators named.

The attack 'writes file 08 or claims condition 4 MET' fails. file 08 measures ff2ebadd…, matching the pin, and git reports it unmodified in my working tree. Condition 4 stays PARTLY MET in clause 3 and in the readiness effect, which also carries 'Condition 5 remains NOT MET and last.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED / QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED' fails on a line-by-line audit of the turn-3 text: SATISFIED negated three times, QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED both inside 'Does not claim', and the MET occurrences are 'Does not make condition 4 MET', 'stays PARTLY MET' twice, 'still not MET' and 'Condition 5 remains NOT MET'. No status token is coined or elevated.
The attack 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fails: both occurrences are refusals and the rejected alternative survives.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on every row this time. COORD 236a97fa…, file 08 ff2ebadd…, v3 b5236612…, my v3 verdict ba7f48c3…, the Codex v3 verdict b5162d99… hashed without opening, the two frozen subjects, and all four reviewer verdicts. Both commits resolve: 75c981dd… to D-056 and 953b2311… to 'D-087: remove duplicate D-056 heading'.

The entry's account of my two prior verdicts is exact: turn 1 as OBJECT with 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX D086-SF-1, and turn 2 as OBJECT with 2 MUST-FIX D086-T2-MF-1 and D086-T2-MF-2 and 1 SHOULD-FIX D086-T2-SF-1. The turn-1 recital compresses away the note count and Codex's zero counts, but D086-N-1 retains its own disposition row and CONSENT entails those zeros, so no finding is dropped.

The new rejected alternative 'Adopt the turn-2 subject. Rejected: dispatch defect (working notes and wrong peer digest)' correctly records why the defective draft is not the adopting text, which is the right way to leave a superseded turn on the record rather than quietly replacing it.
D-086 is still absent from COORD, so adoption creates no collision, and no turn-3 Codex verdict file exists at review time.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing. Both frozen prior subjects, file 08 and COORD are unmodified in my working tree.

The entry's accounts of Codex's positions, including CONSENT at turn 1 and 'OBJECTIONS, 2 MUST-FIX ADV-D086-T2-01 / ADV-D086-T2-02' at turn 2, and its claim that those two findings map onto the same repairs as mine, are all unverified by me.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Every finding I raised across two turns is repaired, and the repairs are the ones I asked for rather than paraphrases: the rider scoped and the two v3 refusals named as retained, the denominators named in clause 3 with the edit honestly recorded, the working notes deleted, the peer digest corrected to a value I re-derived myself, and the re-measure clause restored. The part worth stating is that this turn added two new peer-verdict pins while repairing a mis-pinned one, which is exactly where a repair turn tends to reintroduce the defect it is fixing; I hashed all four and they hold. Clauses 2 and 3 and the rider never entered the diff, so the arithmetic and the scoping stand on the verification I did when they were first written rather than on a fresh reading of unchanged text. What remains is bookkeeping — one note ID absent from the disposition table whose substance was nonetheless fixed — and it does not warrant a fourth turn.
